taskDescription: Click every bone that still contains red marrow in a healthy adult.
textField: In a healthy adult, the *vertebrae*, *sternum*, *ribs*, *pelvis* and *skull* contain red marrow. The proximal *femur* and *humerus* also retain some. The shafts of the tibia and radius hold yellow marrow. The bones of the hands and feet convert to yellow marrow earliest in childhood.

overallFeedback.feedback: By about age 20, red (haematopoietic) marrow is confined to the axial skeleton — vertebrae, sternum, ribs, skull and pelvis — and the proximal ends of the femur and humerus; the rest contains yellow (fatty) marrow, which is why the posterior iliac crest of the pelvis is the standard site for marrow aspiration and trephine biopsy.
